title: Lois and Eunice (2 Timothy 1:3–7)
hookLine: Timothy's faith came through his grandmother and mother; God gives a spirit of power, love and a sound mind
tomorrow: a dying man's last requests: his coat, and his books?

cards: The box says KITCHEN, but there's no kitchen in it. Under the tape: a cracked recipe card, an old church bulletin, a Bible gone soft at the corners, somebody's handwriting in the margins.
Plenty of families have a box like that. Timothy's story has one too, in a way. A letter is on its way to him.
He's a church leader now, and the writer remembers his tears. Then, in the opening lines, the letter reaches back into a house nobody describes, and names two women.

teach.h: DWELT FIRST IN LOIS AND EUNICE.
teach.b: Here's the verse: "When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also." Lois, a grandmother.
Eunice, a mother. Two names, one verse, and the letter says nothing more about them. Unfeigned means not pretend.
Real. And look at the word dwelt. Faith lived in a grandmother first, then a mother, then a son.
It moved in the way people move into a house: it made a home. Grandmother, mother, son: the verse traces it like a family tree, and nobody in it is well-known.
Later the letter adds, "from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures." Nobody argues Timothy into it here. He grew up inside it.
Then a push: "stir up the gift of God, which is in thee." A gift can be real and still burn low.
And then the line Timothy needed: "For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind."
Fear named, and set aside. Power, to act. Love, to aim the power.
A sound mind, to steady both. Lois and Eunice never speak in the letter. But the faith they lived is the reason Timothy is standing there at all.

how: Some churches remember Lois and Eunice when giving thanks for grandparents and parents who pass on faith, and 2 Timothy 1:7 is a verse some Christians hold on to in anxious times.

games.q: who's in the verse — tap the pairs.

s: the Bible tells long stories about Lois and Eunice
they're named in one verse, 2 Timothy 1:5, for an unfeigned faith.
the letter says God hath not given us the spirit of fear
"but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind."
unfeigned faith means a faith with no doubts

games.q: your friend's grandma taught her to pray as a kid. now she's unsure what she believes and feels she's failing her grandma. what does 2 Timothy 1 do with a faith burning low?
o: stir up the gift: a gift can be real and still burn low.
say it's gone for good, so it was never real to begin with.
say faith can't pass through a family, so her grandma doesn't matter.
games.why: the letter tells Timothy, whose faith dwelt first in his grandmother and mother, to stir up the gift, and names a spirit not of fear.

practice: Bring to mind one person who handed you something good: a faith, a habit of kindness, a way of praying, a steadiness when things shook.
Write them a short message, even one line, naming what they passed on, and send it now or save it for later. If they've died, write the line anyway, and keep it somewhere you'll see it.

wordCard.voice: Lois and Eunice. Timothy's grandmother and mother in Second Timothy, named for an unfeigned faith that dwelt in them first, and then in him, from a child.

orig.note: Greek: fearfulness, timidity, in 2 Timothy 1:7: the spirit of fear God has not given.

carryVoice: Hold on to this one: not a spirit of fear, but power, love and a sound mind instead. See you tomorrow.
